analysis.one_liner: Tata Power is the Tata Group's listed power utility, running coal and renewable generation, power transmission and distribution, and solar/EPC businesses across India, alongside legacy overseas coal assets tied to a long-running Indonesia dispute.
analysis.whats_happening: Tata Power reported Q2 FY27 (July-Sept 2026) results on 11 November 2026, posting what multiple outlets called its highest-ever quarterly PAT of ₹1,652 crore (up 33% YoY) on revenue of ₹19,886 crore (up 26%). The same day, the board named Sanjay Banga as CEO-designate to succeed Praveer Sinha, and approved a ₹11,871 crore, 1,800 MW pumped-storage project at Shirwata. Separately, a Singapore court on 6 November authorised seizure of shares in two Tata Power subsidiaries linked to a decade-old Indonesian coal arbitration dispute worth over $650 million.
analysis.plain_terms: Profits keep setting records quarter after quarter, yet the stock has fallen for a year and sits more than a quarter below its September 2024 high — that gap is the thing to understand before anything else. Part of the revenue growth is coming from a low-margin coal/trading segment, which dilutes profitability even as the headline numbers look strong. On top of that, a Singapore court has just given a creditor the green light to seize shares in two of the company's overseas units over a coal-pricing dispute dating back to 2010 — a real legal overhang, not a side issue. The company is also spending heavily (₹25,000 crore planned this year) on renewables and storage, which is raising debt while it bets on future growth.
analysis.quarters: Q1 FY27 (Jun-26): PAT attributable to owners ₹1,176 crore, up 11% YoY; revenue ₹19,051 crore, up 5.6%; EBITDA ₹4,249 crore, up 8.1%. Q2 FY27 (Sep-26): most independent sources (SolarQuarter, ScanX, Lakshmishree, GuruFocus) converge on a record PAT of ₹1,652 crore, up 33% YoY, on revenue of ₹19,886 crore, up 26%; EBITDA rose only 5% to ₹4,245 crore. A smaller set of sources (Upstox, Genvest) report a different PAT figure (₹1,366 crore, margin down to 18.7%) — likely a different profit line (e.g., before exceptional items) rather than a wrong number; flagging as an outlier rather than averaging it in. The prior-year comparative PAT also differs across articles (₹919 crore vs ₹1,243 crore depending on publish date), so the YoY % should be read cautiously. More reliable is the segment mix: Generation & Coal revenue jumped 152% YoY but EBITDA only 62% (low-margin, volume-driven), while Transmission & Distribution revenue rose 12% with EBITDA up 24% (margin-led, regulated and more durable), and Renewables grew a modest 4% in revenue with EBITDA up 10% — meaning overall EBITDA growth (5%) badly lagged revenue growth (26%), i.e. margins got diluted by the coal/trading surge, not by the core franchise weakening. Management reiterated FY27 capex guidance of ₹25,000 crore and a 2.5 GW renewable addition target, but H1 additions were only 645 MW, with curtailment rising from 8.8% in Q1 to 11% in Q2 due to transmission evacuation delays.
analysis.performance_read: Over 1 year the stock is down 9.94%, underperforming both the Nifty (-2.84%) and peer NTPC (+0.35%). Over 3 years it is up 36.52%, roughly tracking the Nifty (27.8%) but behind NTPC (39.47%). Over 5 years the gap widens sharply: Tata Power is up 48.98% versus the Nifty's 38.85%, but NTPC has returned 177.12% — more than three times as much. The stock is currently 27.5% below its 27 September 2024 peak of ₹479.69, trading near the lower half of its 52-week range (₹335-459). The only corporate action on record is a 10:1 split in September 2011, already fully reflected in the price series — there has been no recent demerger or bonus that would understate returns, so this is a genuine price decline, not a chart artifact.
analysis.valuation_read: Reported multiples vary noticeably by source and date — P/E ranging roughly 23x to 31x and P/B around 2.7x-3.1x, with ROE estimates between 6% and 11.6% and ROCE around 7-8%. Not verified - exact current P/E depends heavily on source and date, so treat the range rather than any single number as the read. At the upper end of that range, the market is not pricing Tata Power as a cheap regulated utility; it is pricing in future returns from the renewables, storage and pumped-hydro capex pipeline (₹25,000 crore guided for FY27) rather than today's ~10% ROE. Whether that bet pays off is exactly the open question — it is not yet a settled fact either way.
analysis.growth_read: Revenue and PAT are both growing, but the mix matters: the biggest revenue jump came from the Generation & Coal cluster (+152% YoY) which is lower-margin and volume/trading-driven, while the regulated Transmission & Distribution business grew more modestly (+12% revenue) but with better margin expansion (+24% EBITDA). The renewables growth engine — the long-term growth narrative for the stock — is actually running behind its own 2.5 GW FY27 target (only 645 MW added in H1) because of transmission evacuation bottlenecks, with curtailment worsening quarter on quarter. So the growth is real but currently more volume-led and segment-skewed than a clean margin-led story.
analysis.health_read: Net external debt rose to ₹62,681 crore (from ₹61,238 crore just one quarter earlier) with net debt/equity around 1.27x, driven by heavy capex. Not verified - a precise operating-cash-flow-to-PAT conversion figure could not be confirmed from available sources, so the degree of cash realisation of reported profit is not independently checked here. The more pressing concern right now is not day-to-day operating risk in the core regulated/renewables businesses (which appear cash generative per segment EBITDA trends) but financial and legal risk: rising leverage funding an aggressive capex plan, plus a live, decade-old overseas coal dispute that a Singapore court has just escalated by authorising seizure of shares in two wholly-owned subsidiaries.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoter holding (Tata Sons) has been steady at roughly 46.9% across recent quarters with 0% promoter pledge — a clean signal on that front. LIC holds about 5.72%, making it the largest disclosed domestic institutional holder; broader FII holding is around 10.1% and mutual funds around 8.75% (Nippon India, Franklin India, Mirae Asset among the larger named holders). No marquee individual investor (the kind tracked for other Tata Power-sized stocks) appears among disclosed holders — worth stating plainly rather than implying one is present.
strengths: Record quarterly PAT of ₹1,652 crore in Q2 FY27, up 33% YoY on the headline cluster of sources
Transmission & Distribution segment EBITDA up 24% YoY on regulated, contracted revenue
Zero promoter pledge with stable Tata Sons holding of ~46.9%
Diversified base across generation, T&D and renewables that management says gives resilient cash flows
watchpoints: Singapore court has authorised seizure of shares in two wholly-owned Tata Power subsidiaries over a >$650 million Indonesian coal arbitration award (Kleros/PT Kaltim Prima Coal dispute)
Net debt climbed to ₹62,681 crore in one quarter with net debt/equity near 1.27x against a ₹25,000 crore FY27 capex plan
Renewable capacity additions (645 MW in H1) are running well behind the 2.5 GW FY27 target, with curtailment worsening from 8.8% to 11% quarter on quarter
CEO transition underway (Sanjay Banga named CEO-designate to succeed Praveer Sinha) — a leadership change to track
analysis.one_thing: How the Singapore court enforcement action against Tata Power's Indonesian coal-linked subsidiaries plays out — alongside progress on cost-linked Mundra tariff renegotiations with more states — will determine whether the legacy thermal/coal overhang finally gets resolved or keeps weighing on an otherwise profit-growing, capex-heavy growth story.
analysis.data_notes: Cross-checked Q2 FY27 results across multiple independent outlets (SolarQuarter, Lapaas Voice, ScanX, Lakshmishree, GuruFocus, Investing.com), which converge on a record ₹1,652 crore PAT; set aside a lower, outlier figure (₹1,366 crore / 18.7% margin, from Upstox/Genvest) that likely reflects a different profit line rather than conflicting fact. Prior-year comparative PAT for the same quarter also varies across sources (₹919 crore vs ₹1,243 crore), suggesting restatement — treat YoY percentages with caution and rely on segment EBITDA trends instead. Valuation ratios (P/E 23x-31x, ROE 6%-11.6%, ROCE 7-8%, net debt/equity 1.27x-1.56x) vary by source and date; used the company's own Q2 FY27-reported net debt/equity of 1.27x as the most current, verified figure. Could not independently verify a single primary-source full-year ROE/ROCE or exact standalone shareholding breakdown.
